sources.entry: Whisk - Keyboard-first clipboard manager with a Liquid Glass panel, filters by source app and content type, and rich previews. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/nathan-poncet/whisk) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]
Whisk - Clipboard manager with a Paste-style panel, pins, search operators, paste stack and rich previews.

summary.one_liner: Whisk is an open-source, keyboard-first clipboard manager for macOS, inspired by Paste, that keeps a searchable history of copied text, links, images, files and colors in a floating bottom panel.
summary.what_it_does: Whisk runs as a macOS menu bar app and records every copy (text, links, images, files, colors), deduplicating and saving them locally in SQLite, newest first. Pressing Shift-Command-V opens a floating panel where clicking or pressing Return pastes a card back, optionally directly into the previous text field when Accessibility access is granted. Search matches content and source application, with operators such as app:, type: and pinned, and chips filter by app and content category. Users can pin items, queue several with a paste stack popped by a global shortcut, paste as plain text or rewritten forms, preview items in a large Quick Look-style view, and drag cards into other apps. Retention, capacity limits, pausing, and per-app exclusions control what is kept, and password managers' concealed content is skipped.
use_cases: keep a searchable history of things I copied on a Mac
paste several copied items in order with a paste stack
find an earlier copied link, snippet or image
exclude password manager or sensitive apps from clipboard history
pin frequently used snippets for reuse
notable: Paste-style bottom panel with Liquid Glass look on macOS 26 and material fallback on earlier systems
Search by content or source app, with operators like app:, type: and pinned
Paste stack: queue cards with Shift-Return and pop them in order with a global shortcut
Built on Clean Architecture with a pure kernel, ports and adapters, and a composition root
Rebindable shortcuts; the global shortcut follows the keyboard layout
caveats: Requires macOS 14 or later; building needs the macOS 26 SDK (Xcode 26+ or matching Command Line Tools), and running tests requires Xcode
Two features send data off-device by design: link previews fetch metadata from copied URLs, and the update check queries the GitHub releases API (both can be disabled in Settings)
Future items on the roadmap, iCloud sync and an iOS/iPadOS app, are not yet available; shared pinboards are also planned
